claims.text: Controlled carburization followed by nitriding will significantly increase the surface hardness of high-strength steel relative to untreated steel.
Controlled carburization followed by nitriding will significantly improve wear resistance relative to untreated steel.
Controlled carburization followed by nitriding will significantly improve corrosion resistance relative to untreated steel.
The treatment will remain effective on high-strength steel operating at 500–700°C in corrosive environments.
Carburization enriches the steel surface in carbon.
Surface carbon enrichment promotes carbide formation.
Nitriding after carburization develops a nitride diffusion zone.
Nitriding induces compressive residual stresses in the treated surface.
Precise control of treatment time, temperature, and atmosphere can prevent excessive layer thickness.
Precise control of diffusion parameters can minimize treatment-induced embrittlement.
The treatment produces a duplex layer having an outer carburized zone enriched with hard carbides and an inner nitrided zone containing metal nitrides and compressive residual stresses.
The carbide- and nitride-containing zones form a graded, hardened surface layer.
The graded, hardened surface layer improves wear resistance.
The graded, hardened surface layer improves corrosion resistance.
The graded surface layer improves overall mechanical durability.
Untreated high-strength steel has lower surface hardness and greater susceptibility to wear and corrosion than the proposed treated steel.
The treatment should perform reliably under aggressive thermal and chemical conditions with minimal embrittlement when its process parameters are carefully managed.
Diffusion-based surface treatments are well established.
